audit_status.source_base: ChatGPT-authored Psalms completion draft using public-domain KJV as familiar alignment scaffold with curated Hebrew/textual overrides; full WLC/OSHB/source-witness audit pending
audit_status.review_note: Corrupt rulers/judges, venom, broken teeth, miscarriage imagery, vengeance, and justice.

verses.restored: Do you indeed speak righteousness, O mighty ones [wording uncertain]? Do you judge uprightly, children of humanity?

familiar.text: Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?

notes.title: Difficult opening
notes.body: The Hebrew opening is textually and lexically difficult; translations range from “congregation” to “mighty ones/gods” and other reconstructions. The restored line flags rather than conceals the uncertainty.

modern.text: Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?

original.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אַל תַּשְׁחֵ֗ת לְדָוִ֥ד מִכְתָּֽם הַֽאֻמְנָ֗ם אֵ֣לֶם צֶ֭דֶק תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן מֵישָׁרִ֥ים תִּ֝שְׁפְּט֗וּ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם

verses.restored: Yea, in heart ye work wickedness; ye weigh the violence of your hands in the earth.

familiar.text: Yea, in heart ye work wickedness; ye weigh the violence of your hands in the earth.

modern.text: No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.

original.text: אַף בְּלֵב֮ עוֹלֹ֪ת תִּפְעָ֫ל֥וּן בָּאָ֡רֶץ חֲמַ֥ס יְ֝דֵיכֶ֗ם תְּפַלֵּֽסֽוּן

verses.restored: The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.

familiar.text: The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.

modern.text: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.

original.text: זֹ֣רוּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מֵרָ֑חֶם תָּע֥וּ מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן דֹּבְרֵ֥י כָזָֽב

verses.restored: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: they are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear;

familiar.text: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: they are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear;

modern.text: Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,

original.text: חֲמַת לָ֗מוֹ כִּדְמ֥וּת חֲמַת נָחָ֑שׁ כְּמוֹ פֶ֥תֶן חֵ֝רֵ֗שׁ יַאְטֵ֥ם אָזְנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely.

familiar.text: Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely.

modern.text: refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.

original.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא יִ֭שְׁמַע לְק֣וֹל מְלַחֲשִׁ֑ים חוֹבֵ֖ר חֲבָרִ֣ים מְחֻכָּֽם

verses.restored: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: break out the great teeth of the young lions, O YHWH.

familiar.text: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: break out the great teeth of the young lions, O LORD.

modern.text: O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.

original.text: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים הֲרָס שִׁנֵּ֥ימוֹ בְּפִ֑ימוֹ מַלְתְּע֥וֹת כְּ֝פִירִ֗ים נְתֹ֣ץ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Let them melt away as waters which run continually: when he bendeth his bow to shoot his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.

familiar.text: Let them melt away as waters which run continually: when he bendeth his bow to shoot his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.

modern.text: May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.

original.text: יִמָּאֲס֣וּ כְמוֹ מַ֭יִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ לָ֑מוֹ יִדְרֹ֥ךְ חצו כְּמ֣וֹ יִתְמֹלָֽלוּ

verses.restored: As a snail which melteth, let every one of them pass away: like the untimely birth of a woman, that they may not see the sun.

familiar.text: As a snail which melteth, let every one of them pass away: like the untimely birth of a woman, that they may not see the sun.

notes.title: Miscarriage imagery
notes.body: The psalm uses shocking imprecatory images, including a pregnancy-loss image. Such language belongs to rage poetry and must not be used to stigmatize miscarriage, infertility, pregnancy loss, or children.

modern.text: Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.

original.text: כְּמ֣וֹ שַׁ֭בְּלוּל תֶּ֣מֶס יַהֲלֹ֑ךְ נֵ֥פֶל אֵ֝֗שֶׁת בַּל חָ֥זוּ שָֽׁמֶשׁ

verses.restored: Before your pots can feel the thorns, he shall take them away as with a whirlwind, both living, and in his wrath.

familiar.text: Before your pots can feel the thorns, he shall take them away as with a whirlwind, both living, and in his wrath.

modern.text: Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.

original.text: בְּטֶ֤רֶם יָבִ֣ינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶ֣ם אָטָ֑ד כְּמוֹ חַ֥י כְּמוֹ חָ֝ר֗וֹן יִשְׂעָרֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.

familiar.text: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.

modern.text: The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.

original.text: יִשְׂמַ֣ח צַ֭דִּיק כִּי חָזָ֣ה נָקָ֑ם פְּעָמָ֥יו יִ֝רְחַ֗ץ בְּדַ֣ם הָרָשָֽׁע

verses.restored: So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.

familiar.text: So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.

modern.text: Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”

original.text: וְיֹאמַ֣ר אָ֭דָם אַךְ פְּרִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֑יק אַ֥ךְ יֵשׁ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים שֹׁפְטִ֥ים בָּאָֽרֶץ

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: This is extreme imprecatory poetry. It must never authorize mutilation, killing, harm to children, pregnancy-loss stigma, or celebration of real bloodshed.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
